projects.title: Kosaraju's Algorithm for Strongly Connected Components (SCC)
projects.description: A Strongly Connected Component (SCC) in a directed graph is a maximal set of vertices where every vertex is reachable from any other vertex. Kosaraju's algorithm computes all SCCs in two DFS passes: 1) Run DFS on original graph to get finish times stack; 2) Transpose graph edges `u → v` to `v → u`; 3) Run DFS on transposed graph in order of stack finish times in `O(V + E)` time! In this project, you will build Kosaraju SCC Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Kosaraju 2-Pass DFS, Graph Transposition `v → u` & Strongly Connected Component Discovery
projects.exampleText: Find SCCs in directed graph using Kosaraju's algorithm
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Kosaraju's SCC Algorithm ---
Strongly Connected Components (SCCs): [ {0, 1, 2}, {3}, {4, 5} ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Pass 1 DFS**: Push vertices onto stack upon completing DFS subtree (finish times).
2. **Pass 2 Transpose DFS**: Pop stack; launch DFS on transposed graph to extract individual SCCs.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `kosaraju_scc_demo()`: Computes strongly connected components using Kosaraju's algorithm.

projects.title: Tarjan's Strongly Connected Components Algorithm (DFS Low-Link Stack)
projects.description: Tarjan's SCC algorithm finds all Strongly Connected Components in a directed graph in a SINGLE O(V + E) DFS pass using a Low-Link array `low[u] = min(tin[u], tin[v])` and an explicit node recursion stack! In this project, you will build Tarjan's SCC Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Tarjan's Low-Link Values, Single-Pass DFS Acceleration & Component Stack Popping
projects.exampleText: Find SCCs in directed graph using Tarjan's algorithm
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Tarjan's SCC Algorithm (Low-Link Stack) ---
Strongly Connected Components (Tarjan's): [ {0, 1, 2}, {3}, {4, 5} ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Low-Link Recurrence**: Track `tin[u]` and `low[u]`. Push node onto active recursion stack.
2. **SCC Root Test**: If `low[u] == tin[u]`, pop stack until `u` is popped; elements form an SCC.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `tarjan_scc_demo()`: Computes strongly connected components using Tarjan's algorithm.

projects.title: Condensation Graph Construction from SCCs
projects.description: The Condensation Graph contracts every Strongly Connected Component (SCC) into a single meta-vertex `C_i`. Inter-SCC directed edges form a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)! Enables solving hard graph problems on DAGs in `O(V + E)` time. In this project, you will build DAG Condensation Graph Generator in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Graph Contraction Mechanics, Meta-Node Aggregation & DAG Condensation Invariants
projects.exampleText: Contract SCCs into DAG condensation graph
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Condensation Graph Construction ---
Created DAG Condensation Graph with 3 Meta-Nodes and 2 Directed Edges.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Meta-Node Map**: Map each vertex `v` to its SCC ID `scc_id[v]`.
2. **Edge Compression**: Add directed edge `scc_id[u] → scc_id[v]` if `scc_id[u] != scc_id[v]`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `condensation_graph_demo()`: Constructs DAG condensation graph from graph SCCs.

projects.title: Ford-Fulkerson Method for Maximum Flow
projects.description: The Ford-Fulkerson method computes the maximum possible flow from source node `S` to sink node `T` in a flow network. Repeatedly find an augmenting path in the **Residual Graph** using DFS/BFS and push bottleneck capacity flow `f += bottleneck` until no augmenting paths exist! In this project, you will build Ford-Fulkerson Max-Flow Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Ford-Fulkerson Method, Residual Graph Maintenance & Bottleneck Flow Augmentation
projects.exampleText: Compute maximum flow value from source to sink
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Ford-Fulkerson Method for Maximum Flow ---
Maximum Flow Value (Ford-Fulkerson) = 23
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Residual Network**: Maintain residual capacity `cap[u][v] - flow[u][v]`.
2. **Augment Path**: Find path `S → T` with capacity > 0; add bottleneck flow to forward edges and subtract from reverse edges.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `ford_fulkerson_demo()`: Computes maximum network flow using Ford-Fulkerson method.

projects.title: Edmonds-Karp Algorithm for Maximum Flow (BFS Shortest Augmenting Path)
projects.description: Edmonds-Karp is an implementation of the Ford-Fulkerson method that uses **BFS** (Breadth-First Search) to ALWAYS choose the shortest augmenting path (fewest edges) from `S` to `T`. Guarantees upper bound complexity of `O(V E^2)` independent of edge capacity values! In this project, you will build Edmonds-Karp Max-Flow Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Edmonds-Karp Algorithm, BFS Shortest Augmenting Paths & Polynomial O(V E^2) Guarantees
projects.exampleText: Compute maximum flow via Edmonds-Karp BFS algorithm
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Edmonds-Karp Algorithm for Maximum Flow (BFS) ---
Maximum Flow Value (Edmonds-Karp BFS) = 23 (Completed in O(V E^2) time).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **BFS Augment Search**: Run BFS to locate shortest path from source to sink in residual network.
2. **Bottleneck Push**: Push bottleneck capacity along shortest path until no BFS path exists.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `edmonds_karp_demo()`: Solves maximum flow using Edmonds-Karp BFS algorithm.

projects.title: Dinic's Algorithm for Maximum Network Flow (Level Graph + Blocking Flow)
projects.description: Dinic's algorithm speeds up maximum flow computation to `O(V^2 E)` (and `O(E sqrt(V))` on unit networks) using: 1) **Level Graph** constructed via BFS; 2) **Blocking Flow** pushed via DFS along level graph paths. In this project, you will build Dinic's Max-Flow Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dinic's Algorithm, Level Graph Construction & Blocking Flow DFS Pushes
projects.exampleText: Compute maximum flow via Dinic's level graph algorithm
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Dinic's Algorithm for Maximum Network Flow ---
Maximum Flow Value (Dinic Level Graph) = 23 (Completed in O(V^2 E) time).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Level Graph BFS**: Compute node distance levels `level[u]` from source `S`.
2. **Blocking Flow DFS**: Push flow along edges satisfying `level[v] == level[u] + 1` until no path exists.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `dinic_algorithm_demo()`: Solves maximum network flow using Dinic's level graph algorithm.

projects.title: Minimum Cut Representation via Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem
projects.description: The Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem states that the maximum flow value from S to T equals the minimum capacity of an S-T cut (set of edges whose removal disconnects S from T). Compute Max-Flow, then run BFS from source S in final residual graph: reachable nodes form S-side set, unreachable nodes form T-side set! In this project, you will build Min-Cut Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem, S-T Cut Identification & Residual Graph Reachability
projects.exampleText: Find minimum cut capacity and partition node sets
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Max-Flow Execution**: Run Max-Flow algorithm to saturation.
2. **Residual BFS**: Reachable nodes from `S` in residual graph belong to `S_set`; cut edges cross `S_set → T_set`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_cut_demo()`: Solves Minimum Cut using Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem.

projects.title: Maximum Bipartite Matching via Hopcroft-Karp / Max-Flow
projects.description: Find maximum matching in a bipartite graph (sets L and R). Construct flow network: connect super-source `S` to all nodes in L (capacity 1), bipartite edges from L to R (capacity 1), and all nodes in R to super-sink `T` (capacity 1). Max Flow equals Maximum Bipartite Matching in O(V E) time! In this project, you will build Bipartite Matching Flow Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Bipartite Matching Reduction, Super-Source/Sink Extensions & Unit Flow Networks
projects.exampleText: Find maximum bipartite matching pairs count via Max-Flow
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Maximum Bipartite Matching via Max-Flow ---
Maximum Bipartite Matching Pairs Count = 4
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Super-Nodes**: Add `S` with capacity 1 to set L; add `T` with capacity 1 from set R.
2. **Max-Flow Match**: Run Dinic/Edmonds-Karp; non-zero flow edges indicate matching pairs.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bipartite_matching_flow_demo()`: Solves Maximum Bipartite Matching using Max-Flow.

projects.title: 2-SAT Problem Solver via SCCs
projects.description: The 2-Satisfiability (2-SAT) problem determines if boolean variables can satisfy a 2-CNF formula `(A or B) and (C or D)...`. Construct Implication Graph `~A → B` and `~B → A`. Find SCCs: formula is SATISFIABLE if and only if NO variable `x` and its negation `~x` belong to the same SCC! In this project, you will build 2-SAT Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: 2-SAT Implication Graphs, Logic Clause Extensions & SCC Contradiction Audits
projects.exampleText: Solve 2-SAT boolean formula satisfiability
projects.exampleOutput:
--- 2-SAT Problem Solver via SCCs ---
2-SAT Formula Satisfiable: YES
Variable Assignment: [ x1=TRUE, x2=FALSE, x3=TRUE ]
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Implication Graph**: Convert clause `(u or v)` into directed edges `~u → v` and `~v → u`.
2. **Contradiction Test**: If `scc_id[x] == scc_id[~x]`, formula is UNSATISFIABLE.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `two_sat_scc_demo()`: Solves 2-SAT problem using SCC implication graph analysis.

projects.title: Check 2-Vertex / 2-Edge Connectivity in Graph
projects.description: Verify if a graph is 2-Edge-Connected (remains connected after removing any 1 edge) or 2-Vertex-Connected (biconnected). Check that graph contains NO bridges using Tarjan's Low-Link DFS in O(V + E) time! In this project, you will build Graph Biconnectivity Verifier in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Biconnectivity Properties, 2-Edge Connectivity & Bridge-Free Graph Proofs
projects.exampleText: Verify 2-edge connectivity of undirected graph
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Check 2-Vertex / 2-Edge Connectivity ---
Is Graph 2-Edge-Connected (Biconnected): YES
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Bridge Verification**: Run Tarjan's bridge finder algorithm.
2. **Biconnectivity**: Graph is 2-edge-connected if zero bridges exist.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `vertex_edge_connectivity_demo()`: Verifies graph biconnectivity and 2-edge connectivity.

projects.title: Push-Relabel / Preflow-Push Algorithm for Maximum Flow
projects.description: Push-Relabel (Preflow-Push) works locally instead of searching global augmenting paths. Maintains node height labels `h[u]` and excess flows `excess[u]`. Executes `Push` operations to push excess flow to lower height neighbors and `Relabel` operations to raise node heights in `O(V^3)` time! In this project, you will build Push-Relabel Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Push-Relabel Architecture, Preflow Excess Push & Height Relabeling Operations
projects.exampleText: Compute maximum flow via Push-Relabel algorithm
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Push-Relabel / Preflow-Push Algorithm ---
Maximum Flow Value (Push-Relabel) = 23 (Completed in O(V^3) time).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Preflow Initialization**: Push capacity flow out of source S to adjacent nodes.
2. **Push/Relabel Loop**: While excess flow exists, push flow to lower height neighbor `h[v] == h[u] - 1` or relabel `h[u] = 1 + min(h[neighbors])`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `push_relabel_demo()`: Solves maximum flow using Push-Relabel algorithm.

projects.title: Minimum Cost Maximum Flow (MCMF) Engine
projects.description: In Minimum Cost Maximum Flow (MCMF), each edge has both a capacity AND a unit cost. Find path that pushes MAXIMUM flow while MINIMIZING total cost. Use SPFA / Bellman-Ford to locate shortest cost augmenting paths in `O(F * V * E)` time! In this project, you will build Minimum Cost Max Flow Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Minimum Cost Max Flow (MCMF), SPFA Cost Augmentation & Dual Flow-Cost Optimizations
projects.exampleText: Compute maximum flow with minimum cost
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Minimum Cost Maximum Flow (MCMF) Engine ---
Max Flow = 20, Min Cost = 140
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Cost Augmentation**: Find path from source to sink with lowest cost in residual graph using SPFA.
2. **Flow & Cost Accumulation**: Push bottleneck flow; add `bottleneck * path_cost` to total cost.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `mcmf_demo()`: Solves Minimum Cost Maximum Flow (MCMF).

projects.title: Image Segmentation via Min-Cut Max-Flow
projects.description: Image Segmentation partitions pixels into Foreground and Background sets. Model pixels as graph nodes: connect source `S` (foreground weight) and sink `T` (background weight); connect adjacent pixels with boundary penalty capacities. Computing Min-Cut yields optimal image segmentation in `O(V^2 E)` time! In this project, you will build Image Segmentation Min-Cut Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Computer Vision Image Segmentation, Graph Cut Penalties & Min-Cut Foreground Partitioning
projects.exampleText: Partition 2D image pixels into Foreground and Background via Min-Cut
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Image Segmentation via Min-Cut Max-Flow ---
Partitioned 2D image pixels into Foreground and Background sets via Min-Cut.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **S-T Penalties**: Connect source S (foreground likelihood) and sink T (background likelihood).
2. **Min-Cut Separation**: Min-Cut minimizes total foreground/background and boundary penalty costs.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `image_segmentation_mincut_demo()`: Solves image segmentation via Min-Cut Max-Flow.

projects.title: Project Selection Problem (Closure Problem via Min-Cut)
projects.description: Select a subset of projects to maximize profit, where taking project A requires purchasing equipment B (prerequisite dependencies). Connect source S to positive profit projects, negative cost equipment to sink T, and project prerequisites with INF capacity. Max Profit = `Positive Sum - Min-Cut`! In this project, you will build Project Selection Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Project Selection Closure Problems, Prerequisite Infinite Capacities & Max Profit Min-Cut Reduction
projects.exampleText: Calculate maximum profit from project selection with prerequisites
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Project Selection Problem (Closure Problem via Min-Cut) ---
Maximum Profit achievable from selected projects = 150
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Prerequisite Edges**: Add `INF` capacity edge from project `u` to required equipment `v`.
2. **Max Profit Formula**: `MaxProfit = TotalPositiveProfits - MinCutCapacity`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `project_selection_demo()`: Solves Project Selection Problem using Min-Cut.

projects.title: Circulation Problem with Lower Bounds
projects.description: Find flow circulation where each edge requires flow `L[u][v] <= flow[u][v] <= C[u][v]` and net flow at every node is 0. Transform lower bounds: subtract lower bounds `L` from capacities; add demands to supply/demand array; check feasibility via Max-Flow! In this project, you will build Circulation Solver in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Lower Bounded Network Flows, Feasible Circulation Proofs & Supply/Demand Extensions
projects.exampleText: Verify feasibility of circulation flow with lower bounds
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Circulation Problem with Lower Bounds ---
Valid Circulation Flow Found: YES
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Capacity Adjustment**: Modify capacity `C' = C - L`.
2. **Supply/Demand Nodes**: Add extra source/sink; feasible if Max Flow equals sum of positive demands.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `circulation_lower_bounds_demo()`: Solves Circulation Problem with lower bounds.

projects.title: Maximum Weight Bipartite Matching (Hungarian Algorithm / MCMF)
projects.description: Find maximum weight assignment matching in a bipartite graph (e.g. assigning N workers to N jobs with cost matrix `cost[i][j]`). Solve using Hungarian Algorithm or MCMF (Minimum Cost Maximum Flow with inverted negative weights) in `O(V^3)` time! In this project, you will build Hungarian Matching Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Hungarian Algorithm, Dual Matrix Potentials & Bipartite Maximum Weight Matching
projects.exampleText: Compute maximum weight job assignment matching
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Maximum Weight Bipartite Matching (Hungarian Algorithm) ---
Maximum Weight Matching Assignment Cost = 450
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Potential Matrix**: Maintain row/column potential arrays `u[i]` and `v[j]`.
2. **Augmenting Paths**: Find shortest augmenting path in equality graph.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `hungarian_algorithm_demo()`: Solves Maximum Weight Bipartite Matching using Hungarian Algorithm.

projects.title: Maximum Edge-Disjoint Paths in Directed Graph
projects.description: Find maximum number of paths from source S to sink T that do not share any common edges (Edge-Disjoint Paths). Assign unit capacity `1` to all edges in graph; Maximum Flow value equals exact maximum number of edge-disjoint paths! In this project, you will build Edge-Disjoint Paths Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Menger's Theorem, Unit Capacity Networks & Edge-Disjoint Path Extractions
projects.exampleText: Find maximum edge-disjoint paths count from source to sink
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Maximum Edge-Disjoint Paths via Max-Flow ---
Maximum Edge-Disjoint Paths Count = 3
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Unit Capacity Network**: Set capacity = 1 for all graph edges.
2. **Menger's Theorem**: Max Flow equals maximum number of edge-disjoint paths.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `edge_disjoint_paths_flow_demo()`: Solves Maximum Edge-Disjoint Paths via Max-Flow.

projects.title: Minimum Path Cover in Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)
projects.description: Find minimum number of vertex-disjoint paths required to cover all vertices of a DAG. Transform DAG into Bipartite Graph: split each node `u` into `u_in` and `u_out`. Formula: `Min Path Cover = V - Max Bipartite Matching`! In this project, you will build DAG Path Cover Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: DAG Path Covers, Bipartite Node Splitting & Dilworth's Theorem
projects.exampleText: Compute minimum path cover count in DAG
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Minimum Path Cover in DAG (Bipartite Matching Reduction) ---
Minimum Path Cover Count = 2
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Bipartite Node Split**: Create left set `u_out` and right set `v_in`.
2. **Path Cover Formula**: `MinPaths = TotalVertices - MaxBipartiteMatching`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `min_path_cover_dag_demo()`: Solves Minimum Path Cover in DAG via Bipartite Matching.

projects.title: Dinic's Algorithm with Scaling (Bitwise Flow Scaling)
projects.description: Accelerate Dinic's Max-Flow algorithm on large edge capacities using Bitwise Capacity Scaling. Push flow along augmenting paths with capacity `>= Delta` (where Delta starts at MSB power of 2 and divides by 2 each round). Reduces complexity to `O(E^2 log U)`! In this project, you will build Bitwise Flow Scaling Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Bitwise Capacity Scaling, MSB Delta Thresholding & Flow Acceleration
projects.exampleText: Execute Dinic's algorithm with bitwise capacity scaling
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Dinic's Algorithm with Bitwise Flow Scaling ---
Computed Max Flow with Capacity Scaling in O(E^2 log U) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Delta Threshold**: Filter edges during BFS/DFS level graph construction: require `cap >= Delta`.
2. **Bitwise Bit Shift**: Shift `Delta >>= 1` after each scaling phase.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `dinic_scaling_demo()`: Solves Max-Flow using Dinic's algorithm with bitwise flow scaling.

projects.title: Strongly Connected Component Dynamic Condensation Engine
projects.description: Maintain dynamic DAG condensation graphs under real-time edge additions. When a new edge connects two distinct SCCs in reverse topological direction, merge intermediate SCCs into a single combined component! In this project, you will build Dynamic SCC Condensation Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Dynamic SCC Merging, Topological Reverse Cycle Collapse & Dynamic DAG Graphs
projects.exampleText: Re-evaluate DAG condensation graph after dynamic edge insertion
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Strongly Connected Component Dynamic Condensation Engine ---
Re-evaluated DAG condensation graph after dynamic edge insertion.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Cycle Collapse**: Detect cycle formed by new edge across condensation nodes.
2. **Meta-Node Merge**: Merge all nodes on cycle into a single updated meta-node.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `scc_dynamic_condensation_demo()`: Re-evaluates dynamic SCC condensation graph upon edge insertion.

projects.title: Highest-Label Preflow-Push Max-Flow Kernel
projects.description: The Highest-Label Preflow-Push algorithm selects the active node with MAXIMUM height label `h[u]` to push excess flow, achieving optimal time complexity of `O(V^2 sqrt(E))` without dynamic tree data structures! In this project, you will build Highest-Label Max-Flow Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Highest-Label Selection Heuristics, Height Bucket Queues & O(V^2 sqrt(E)) Max-Flow
projects.exampleText: Execute Highest-Label Preflow-Push max flow algorithm
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Highest-Label Preflow-Push Max-Flow Kernel ---
Evaluated Highest-Label Preflow-Push in O(V^2 sqrt(E)) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Height Buckets**: Maintain array of active node lists indexed by height `h[u]`.
2. **Max Height Push**: Always pop active node from highest non-empty height bucket.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `highest_label_push_relabel_demo()`: Implements Highest-Label Preflow-Push max-flow kernel.

projects.title: Gomory-Hu Tree Construction for All-Pairs Min-Cuts
projects.description: A Gomory-Hu Tree represents all `V*(V-1)/2` minimum S-T cuts of an undirected graph using a tree of V nodes! Requires running ONLY `V - 1` Max-Flow computations instead of `V^2`! In this project, you will build Gomory-Hu Tree Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Gomory-Hu Tree Construction, Cut Tree Decompositions & All-Pairs Min-Cut Compressions
projects.exampleText: Construct Gomory-Hu Tree using V-1 Max-Flow computations
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Gomory-Hu Tree Construction for All-Pairs Min-Cuts ---
Constructed Gomory-Hu Tree using V-1 Max-Flow computations.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Recursive Partition**: Pick 2 nodes in same tree partition, compute Min-Cut, and split partition.
2. **V-1 Runs**: Connect contracted nodes with tree edge of capacity equal to Min-Cut.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `gomory_hu_tree_demo()`: Solves Gomory-Hu Tree construction.

projects.title: Cost-Scaling Minimum Cost Flow Engine
projects.description: The Cost-Scaling algorithm solves Minimum Cost Flow in `O(V^2 E log(V * C))` time by maintaining epsilon-optimal flows and halving error parameter `epsilon >>= 1` each phase. In this project, you will build Cost-Scaling MCMF Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Cost-Scaling MCMF, Epsilon-Optimal Pseudoflows & Logarithmic Error Phase Reductions
projects.exampleText: Compute minimum cost flow via cost-scaling algorithm
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Cost-Scaling Minimum Cost Flow Engine ---
Computed Minimum Cost Flow using epsilon-scaling in O(V^2 E log(V C)) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Epsilon Scaling**: Maintain `epsilon`-optimal node potentials `p[u]`.
2. **Refine Phase**: Push flow along admissible edges `c_p(u, v) < 0` and relabel potentials.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `cost_scaling_mcmf_demo()`: Solves Minimum Cost Flow using cost-scaling algorithm.
